guitar.notes: Stevie Ray Vaughan's battered Fender Stratocaster "Number One" is one of the most famous guitars in blues history; this should never have been left unknown since the artist IS the guitarist.

tone.target: Texas blues lead with singing sustain and SRV-style grit
tone.profile: Texas blues lead with singing sustain and SRV-style grit
tone.summary: A vintage, mid-pushed signal chain using a Green OD boost into a US Deluxe amp model, paired with a 2x12 cab, emphasizing vocal sustain and tight low end.

rig.name: Stevie Ray Vaughan - The Sky Is Crying - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Simulate the mid-forward push of a Tube Screamer style boost for grit and sustain.

alternatives.reason: Good alternative, but Green OD is closer to the classic TS sound.

blocks.purpose: Bypass or use for subtle grit if needed (keeping the tone clean and direct).
blocks.gap: The signal path relies heavily on Green OD for gain; no dedicated distortion stage is required.

blocks.purpose: Provide the clean, Fender-style edge and headroom required for blues lead playing.

alternatives.reason: Excellent alternative, but US Deluxe is a strong representation of the desired Fender sound.

blocks.purpose: Match the Fender combo sound and provide a focused, articulate tone.
Fine-tune the mid-range presence and tighten the low end without sounding scooped.
Avoid modulation effects as per the 'avoid' list and focus on direct tone.
blocks.gap: The required effect is Spring Reverb (RVB), not a modulator. This slot is reserved for reverb/ambience.

blocks.purpose: Add the requested touch of classic spring reverb for vintage blues ambiance.

alternatives.reason: Too clean and artificial; Spring is more authentic to the genre.

improvements.summary: Enhance cabinet realism for better articulation and vintage character.

proposals.reason: Improve the natural, open sound of a classic blues combo.
